findings.evidence: `HopfIdealPointsNaturality.lean:67` defines the public `quotientPointsSubgroupFunctor`, and `:96` defines a bundled natural inclusion into ambient points; this PR only adds the pointwise equality at `HopfIdealPointsOrder.lean:95` using `Subgroup.inclusion`, with no `NatTrans`/functor-level inclusion found by `rg "NatTrans|Subgroup.inclusion|inclusion.*Functor|Antitone fun I"`.
findings.fix: Add an exposed bundled definition, e.g. `quotientPointsSubgroupInclusion (H) (hIJ : I ≤ J) : quotientPointsSubgroupFunctor H J ⟶ quotientPointsSubgroupFunctor H I`, with `app A := GrpCat.ofHom (Subgroup.inclusion (quotientPointsSubgroup_le_of_le H hIJ A))`, plus a `[simp]` app lemma; keep the pointwise theorem as its naturality/app API if desired.
findings.issue: `mapQuotientPointsSubgroup_inclusion` proves componentwise naturality of the inclusions but exposes no natural transformation `quotientPointsSubgroupFunctor H J ⟶ quotientPointsSubgroupFunctor H I` for `I ≤ J`, so downstream functor-level closed-subgroup code must rebuild the morphism and its naturality proof.

summary: The pointwise order lemmas are useful, but the public API stops short of the bundled functor-level inclusion needed by the existing closed-subgroup functor interface.
